transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-25 16:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Amy Lee (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Tasha Nguyen (Redwood CSM), Jordan Patel (VP Eng - Sparrow), Priya Menon (SRE), Omar Khan (FinOps), Leah Brooks (Product)

Summary (auto): Quarterly check-in to review usage and spend spike in last 6 weeks; discuss recent latency tail events during evening windows; evaluate dedicated/reserved capacity pilot; align on roadmap items and security deliverables.

00:00 Amy Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we know it's a busy week so we'll try to keep this tight, quick readout on what we've seen then open to Qs
00:18 Jordan Patel: yeah thanks Amy, appreciate it. Our team's been seeing increased api costs and a couple of flares in tail latency, especially after the release of the conversation history feature, so wanted to sync on options
00:37 Marco Ruiz: quick context — we pulled the metrics, your token throughput jumped ~38% month-over-month and peak concurrent requests during UTC evening window doubled, that combined with longer context lengths means more KV cache pressure
00:58 Priya Menon: right, and from SRE side the p99 went from about 420ms to around 1.1s in those windows, sometimes a couple of dropped requests when autoscaling caught up
01:22 Amy Lee: thanks, that's consistent with what we saw in the logs Jordan shared. On the cost side Omar, did you want to surface the FinOps concerns?
01:33 Omar Khan: sure — main issue is unit cost per token jumped because more requests are hitting higher seq-length buckets; plus we had a handful of runaway small-batch requests that weren't being batched well, so your estimate for next quarter looks 30% over plan unless we change config or move some traffic to a cheaper variant
01:55 Leah Brooks: when you say cheaper variant, do you mean downgrading model size or quantization? We care about answer quality for summaries
02:09 Marco Ruiz: two axes — quantized variants and routing to a slightly smaller model for non-critical routes. We can also use prefix caching aggressively on repeated prompts. There's a tradeoff in F1/precision but for summarization often OK with int8 quantized variant
02:38 Jordan Patel: but we'd need assurances on rollback if quality regresses — our Legal/PMO will want regressions to be flagged in staging before any prod rollout
02:52 Amy Lee: absolutely, we recommend a canary rollout and an eval harness that reports BLEU/ROUGE-style deltas on your prompt set; we can tie that to automatic fallback so the original model is used if deltas exceed thresholds
03:12 Priya Menon: security question — for the dedicated pilot we'd need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS, plus audit logs retention for 1 year, is that supported?
03:26 Marco Ruiz: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs can be exported to your S3 bucket with encryption. There's a short setup lead time for KMS key exchange and firewall rules
03:40 Omar Khan: and cost model for dedicated — we need the monthly reserved vs burst pricing clarified. Also curious about predictable throttles if you hit capacity limits; we can't have silent failures
03:53 Amy Lee: for Dedicated we present a reserved capacity commit with baseline throughput and optional burst credits; we also have SLA-backed latency targets and transparent throttling policies (we emit explicit error codes and quota alerts rather than silent drops)
04:12 Jordan Patel: perfect. Can you also run a 24-hour spike test on staging that mirrors our evening UTC peak? We want to see tail behavior under load and to validate autoscaling timings
04:27 Marco Ruiz: yes — if you can share the traffic replay and sample prompt set we'll spin a 24h run both on hosted staging and a dedicated staging variant and share traces plus kernel-level time breakdowns
04:44 Priya Menon: one thing we noticed — a few kube-proxy timeouts were logged during autoscale events. I know Redwood runtime is GPU-optimized but do we have recommended networking settings for k8s when using Private?
04:58 Marco Ruiz: we do — we'v got a playbook. Short answer: increase pod disruption budget, set tcp keepalive longer, and tune lb idle timeouts. We'll send a Private-deploy k8s tuning doc after this call
05:16 Amy Lee: thanks. On roadmap alignment, we have a few items we think will help you: smarter prefix caching, preemptive batch sizing heuristics, and an eval-driven auto-fallback for quality regressions. We'd like to pilot the caching + batch heuristics with Sparrow in Q1
05:36 Leah Brooks: timeline-wise, our product team wants to avoid any user-facing regressions during Q1 marketing push; if the pilot is gated by canary and staging evals we're comfortable moving forward
05:52 Omar Khan: procurement timeline — we aim to make a decision by end of December, procurement needs numbers for committed spend and expected unit costs for both hosted and Dedicated options
06:08 Amy Lee: we'll get you a side-by-side cost comparison and a recommended committed capacity that aligns with your 95th percentile throughput to minimize burst costs
06:22 Jordan Patel: ok good. A few clarifications on SLOs: what are typical p99 numbers for model X on your Dedicated offering?
06:34 Marco Ruiz: depends on sequence length distribution, but for your median context lengths we expect p99 under 300-450ms on Dedicated with proper batching and KV cache warm. We'll include model-specific benchmarks in the materials
06:50 Priya Menon: in the past we also saw an error class from a misaligned kv-cache eviction policy, can that be instrumented more clearly for us?
07:03 Marco Ruiz: yes we can add more fine-grained traces for KV hits/misses and make those available in the console per-route; we'll also set up a tracing hook so SRE can pull spans during incidents
07:18 Amy Lee: quick recap before we move to logistics: action items as noted — Amy to do cost proposal, Marco to run spike test and schedule deep-dive, Priya to provide prompt set, Omar to confirm procurement timeline. Any other asks?
07:36 Jordan Patel: please include a short checklist of security docs (SOC2 scope, encryption at rest/transit, data residency options, audit log retention) with the proposal
07:49 Tasha Nguyen: we'll attach the compliance packet (SOC2, penetration test summary) and a Private-deploy onboarding checklist to the email with proposal
08:04 Leah Brooks: and a sample eval harness with pass/fail thresholds would be very helpful so our PMs can sign off
08:15 Marco Ruiz: noted — we'll include an eval sample and a suggested threshold matrix tuned for your summarization flows
08:28 Amy Lee: ok last item — can we set the follow-up deep-dive for next week? I'm seeing availability Tue/Wed morning PST
08:39 Jordan Patel: Tue morning PST works for us
08:42 Amy Lee: great, Marco will send calendar invite. Thanks everyone, appreciate the productive session
08:51 Omar Khan: thanks all
08:54 Priya Menon: thanks
08:56 Meeting end

Notes on transcript quality: some product names auto-corrected (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K-V cache"), occasional speaker mislabels around crosstalk at 02:30-03:00.

References shared: pricing-scenarios-sparrow.xlsx (drive link), private-deploy-k8s-tuning.pdf (drive link), compliance-packet-redwood.pdf (drive link), sample-eval-harness.zip (drive link).

Requested artifacts to attach after call: detailed cost-savings breakdown, sample pricing for reserved capacity, Private deploy playbook, 24h spike benchmark results, eval harness and threshold matrix.
